messages.content: What is the effect of economic status on happiness levels?

function.name: get_happiness_index

country.description: The country for which to retrieve the happiness index.

year.description: The year for which to retrieve the happiness index.

demographic_group.description: The demographic group for which to retrieve the happiness index. If not specified, the total for all groups will be returned.

message.content: Economic status—often measured by income level or wealth—has a strong influence on happiness, but the relationship is nuanced. In general, higher income allows people to meet basic needs (food, shelter, healthcare) and reduces stress related to financial insecurity, which tends to increase overall life satisfaction. However, once basic needs are met, the incremental benefit of additional income on happiness diminishes; this is known as the “income‑happiness plateau.” Social comparisons also matter: people often gauge their well‑being relative to peers, so relative income can affect perceived happiness even if absolute income is high. Additionally, the way income is used matters—spending on experiences, relationships, or health tends to boost happiness more than material consumption. So while economic status is a key factor, its impact depends on context, relative standing, and how resources are allocated.
